rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single dominant curved bar with a clear hierarchy and good multi-view consistency. The plan/top view confirms the same bent ribbon logic seen in the oblique views, so it avoids the one-view-only problem. The thick blue access edge is not perfectly celebrated, but the form’s concave condition and recess at the ground edge provide a plausible public threshold rather than a sealed frontage. The silhouette is not a repetitive stair stack; it is a continuous curved mass with a slightly stepped/trimmed top condition that still reads as one form. Programmatically, this is plausible for neighborhood living because it suggests a compact mixed-use street building with a legible ground response and a calm upper mass. Sectionally, it is somewhat limited because the roof/section is mostly a smooth extruded bend rather than a clearly articulated inhabited terrace or daylight-driven section, so it is only moderately strong there. Overall, it resonates most with the similar references’ principles of courtyard/void and continuous curved mass without copying them.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Curved upper mass with a substantial courtyard-like void and a bridge/connector that keeps the ground edge legible.
